mu_name_from: VersionSeasonSix/Items/Orbs.cs:45 -- CreateOrb(14, SkillNumber.SwellLife, 1, "Orb of Greater Fortitude", 60, 120, ..., 43000): MU's name, drop level, level and price. Its number is ours: 12/14 is the Wings of Soul here (content/items/wings/Wing05.json), so it takes 29, the first free on main and on the darklord branch.
why_this_one:
The knight's Swell Life, which this game did not have (Discord, 2026-10-25: "there's no orb of greater fortitude in the game? the hp buff for bk"). Read once, the skill is his for good (docs/game/skills-dk.md SS3.3).

Where it falls: drop level 60, MU's, so off any monster of level 60 or more (Realm::kill's reaches) -- Lost Tower's deep floors (Devil, Death Knight, Death Gorgon, Balrog), Atlans' (Bahamut, Silver Valkyrie, Lizard King, Hydra), Blood Castle from its third door, Devil Square, Tarkan, Icarus, Aida and Kanturu, and Lorencia's Golden Dragon. The same ground as the Orb of Death Stab's, its tier. Never in a shop, as no knight orb is.

Who reads it: the knight alone, as MU's CharacterClasses.AllKnights -- the Magic Gladiator has no Swell Life in MU. At level 120: MU's own, which is also our orbs' ladder of twice the drop level. No stat asked: what it gives grows with energy and vitality (sim::swellShare), so asking them would charge twice.
mesh_note: No geometry of its own. Gem01.bmd through Gem05.bmd are byte-identical in MuMain's Data/Item -- one md5 across all five -- so every orb in MU is one model told apart by its row, and this names the one the pipeline has built.

stats.note: An orb has no damage roll and no hand: it is a Prize and nothing else, and the shape of the row is the elf orbs' own (Version075/Items/Orbs.cs:63-67) -- one cell, durability one, dropped by monsters.
stats.durability_note: One. One reading, as a scroll is.
stats.classes_from: CharacterClasses.AllKnights (VersionSeasonSix/Items/Orbs.cs:45). The knight's alone; Prize.ReadBy refuses the rest whatever their level.
stats.requires_note: What the character must BE to read it. Carried raw: docs/reference/mu-scrolls-and-orbs.md SS4 establishes that a non-wearable row's requirement is used verbatim rather than run through `(3 x drop level x raw / 100) + 20`, and sim/items.cpp's `asks` already takes `need_level` unscaled. The same number is on the skill block below, which is what Realm::useItem checks -- the two must agree, and a row where they do not is a transcription error caught for free.

skill.note: What the orb teaches. Read once and gone -- the durability of one is what 'used once' means on this row.
skill.name: Swell Life
skill.tells: His party's most health raised for five minutes, him with them. The keener and hardier the knight, and the more of them near him, the more.
skill.tells_from: The skill's own line in sim/skills.cpp, kept letter for letter so the orb's tooltip and the skill's card cannot say different things about the same blow. MU never prints a line like this at all; it is ours, as it is on the elf's orbs.
skill.energy_from: None. The knight's skills carry no energy requirement in 0.75 -- CreateSkill is called with mana and nothing else for all six (Version075/SkillsInitializer.cs:58-63) -- and gating them behind the stats that make them good would charge twice (docs/game/skills-dk.md SS3.3).
skill.level_from: Ours: about twice the scroll's drop level, in MU's own order (the user's audit of 2026-10-02: 'currently chars can get end game scroll and orbs pretty fast, remember we have 100% exp rate'). At kExperienceRate 100 a character who never leaves Lorencia reaches level 60 in about a hundred kills and 120 in about sixteen hundred, so MU's own gates -- energy alone on a scroll, the drop level on an orb -- fell within minutes. The energy (or other stat) MU asks is kept beside it.
